Hi,

By coincidence, here is a raster implementation of ggmap :)
https://github.com/kohske/ggmap/tree/feature/raster

One point:
using data.frame like (x=long, y=lat, fill = z) is time-consuming in
some situations.
For example, on the flow of
1) getting google map image as jpeg
2) read it into imagematrix (3D array for colour image and 2D matrix
for greyscale image)
3) melt the imagematrix into the long format data frame: this is time-consuming.
4) pass the long-format data frame to geom_raster.

So maybe it is preferable if we have an option such as,
(xmin = long.ll, ymin = lat.ll, xmax=long.ur, ymax=lat.ur, image = foo),
where foo is "a pointer" to the imagematrix or something.

But obviously, the problem is what form should be the pointer.

thanks,

kohske

messages.subject: Re: geom_raster and annotation_raster
parts: > Are you looking for annotation_raster?>

Yes, just after I sent the e-mail ;-p

But, say, I imagine this kind of plot:

library(ggplot2) # latest version
library(ggmap) # from kohske@github

r1 <- ggmap("tokyo")
r2 <- ggmap("kyoto")

attr(r1, "bb") <- data.frame(attr(r1, "bb"), loc = "Tokyo")
attr(r2, "bb") <- data.frame(attr(r2, "bb"), loc = "Kyoto")

ggplot() +
geom_raster(aes(xmin = ll.lon, xmax = ur.lon, ymin = ll.lat, ymax =
ur.lat), data = attr(r1, "bb"), image = r1) +
geom_raster(aes(xmin = ll.lon, xmax = ur.lon, ymin = ll.lat, ymax =
ur.lat), data = attr(r2, "bb"), image = r2) +
coord_equal() + facet_wrap(~loc, scales = "free") + opts(aspect.ratio=1)

it can not be done with annotation_raster.
but maybe can be done with geom_raster in ggplot2.

anyway, it is just for performance tuning, so not in the urgent todos.

messages.author: deb55ea526b6a46e
parts:
This is my first post to this website.  I only recently started using ggplot and am loving it.  I have encountered a problem I don't know how to overcome or have the vocabulary around to search the archives appropriately.  

I have some data of people in a classroom and am plotting a dotplot (or something like that).  I want to see the mean of each person (which I can) and group the people together in a facet by sex.  I can do this but all people show up in both sections/panels of the facet.  How can I get just males and just females in each panel?

wc.mean.pol2<-structure(list(person = c("Ari", "Emma", "Halley", "Howard", 
"Harry", "John", "Kelly", "Marge", "Susan", "Jake", "Juan", "Jose", 
"Stew", "Sherry", "Norah", "Cheryl"), sex = structure(c(1L, 1L, 
1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 1L, 1L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 2L, 1L, 1L, 1L), .Label = c("f", 
"m"), class = "factor"), role = c("student", "student", "student", 
"student", "student", "student", "student", "student", "researcher", 
"teacher", "student", "student", "student", "student", "student", 
"student"), total.wc = c(67, 76, 131, 41, 35, 357, 26, 47, 99, 
2102, 68, 73, 17, 124, 166, 74), mean.polarity = c(-0.029, 0.036, 
0.019, 0.3, 0, 0.527, 0.5, 0.25, -0.008, 0.537, 0.24, 0.02, -0.074, 
0.258, 0.012, 0.06)), .Names = c("person", "sex", "role", "total.wc", 
"mean.polarity"), row.names = c(NA, -16L), class = "data.frame")

DP<-qplot(mean.polarity, person, data=wc.mean.pol2)
DP + geom_point(aes(colour = sex)) + facet_grid(sex~.) 

Cheers
Tyler Rinker

messages.author: 27405c4b711a1080
messages.subject: Re:
parts:
Tyler, 

Firstly, thanks so much for the reproducible example!

Secondly. 

DP + geom_point(aes(colour = sex)) + facet_grid(sex~., scales="free")

Setting the scales free eliminates unused factor levels on an axis. You can specify "free_y" if you don't want the x-axis to shift (it doesn't in your example). 

HTH, 

Brandon

On Fri, Dec 2, 2011 at 05:00, Tyler Rinker <tyler_...@hotmail.com> wrote:
DP<-qplot(mean.polarity, person, data=wc.mean.pol2)
DP + geom_point(aes(colour = sex)) + facet_grid(sex~.)
